title: Thermal Energy Transfer: Effects and Modes
topic: Transfer of Thermal Energy and its Effects
subject: Science

questions.question: Which statement best describes how thermal energy is transferred through a metal rod by conduction?
options: Thermal energy moves through the metal as a fluid flow
Thermal energy is passed along through direct contact within the material
Thermal energy travels as waves through empty space in the metal
Thermal energy is carried by moving currents inside the solid
questions.explanation: Conduction is the transfer of thermal energy through direct contact within a material. In metals, thermal energy is passed efficiently from the hot end to the cold end through the material itself.

questions.question: Why does thermal energy transfer by convection only occur in fluids (liquids and gases)?
options: Fluids can flow and move, allowing warmer regions to rise and cooler regions to sink
Fluids are always hotter than solids
Fluids absorb radiation better than solids
Fluids conduct thermal energy faster than solids
questions.explanation: Convection requires the movement of the substance itself. In fluids, warmer regions become less dense and rise, while cooler, denser regions sink, creating a circulation current that transfers thermal energy.

questions.question: Which property allows thermal energy from the Sun to reach Earth through empty space?
options: Conduction through space
Convection currents in space
Radiation can travel without needing a material medium
Evaporation of solar material
questions.explanation: Radiation is the transfer of thermal energy that does not require a material medium. It can travel through empty space, which is how thermal energy from the Sun reaches Earth.

questions.question: What is one effect when a metal bridge gains thermal energy on a hot day?
options: The bridge contracts and becomes shorter
The bridge expands and may increase in length
The bridge changes state from solid to liquid
The bridge emits less radiation
questions.explanation: When materials gain thermal energy, they generally expand. Solids like metal bridges increase in length when heated, which is why expansion joints are built into structures to allow for this change.

questions.question: Which material is MOST suitable for the handle of a cooking pot to minimise thermal energy transfer to the hand?
options: Aluminium
Copper
Thick plastic with trapped air
Stainless steel
questions.explanation: Plastic with trapped air is a poor conductor of thermal energy. Both plastic and air transfer thermal energy slowly, reducing the rate at which thermal energy reaches the hand and preventing burns.

questions.question: How does a vacuum flask reduce thermal energy transfer to keep a hot drink warm?
options: The vacuum allows conduction but blocks convection and radiation
The vacuum blocks conduction and convection; shiny walls reflect radiation back
The plastic stopper conducts thermal energy away from the drink
The glass inner wall absorbs all radiation
questions.explanation: A vacuum has no material to transfer thermal energy by conduction or convection. The shiny surfaces reflect radiation back into the liquid. Together, these features minimise all three modes of thermal energy transfer.

questions.question: When a substance gains thermal energy, what generally happens to its size?
options: Most substances become smaller
Most substances expand and take up more space
The size does not change at all
Only liquids change size, solids and gases do not
questions.explanation: Generally, solids, liquids and gases expand when they gain thermal energy and contract when they give out thermal energy. This change in size is called thermal expansion.

questions.question: In a room with a heater placed near the floor, why does thermal energy spread throughout the room over time?
options: Thermal energy is conducted rapidly through the air from floor to ceiling
Warm air near the heater rises and cooler air sinks to replace it, creating a circulation current
Radiation from the heater pushes air molecules directly upward
Air particles evaporate and carry thermal energy upward
questions.explanation: Air near the heater gains thermal energy, becomes less dense, and rises. Cooler, denser air sinks to take its place. This continuous circulation—a convection current—distributes thermal energy throughout the room.

questions.question: Why does a dull black surface feel warmer than a shiny white surface when both are exposed to sunlight for the same time?
options: Dull black surfaces conduct thermal energy better than shiny white surfaces
Dull black surfaces absorb more radiation; shiny white surfaces reflect more
Shiny white surfaces create stronger convection currents
Dull black surfaces produce thermal energy through chemical reactions
questions.explanation: Dark, dull surfaces are good absorbers of radiation—they take in more incoming radiation and convert it to thermal energy, raising their temperature. Light, shiny surfaces reflect more radiation away, so they gain less thermal energy and feel cooler.

questions.question: A student places identical metal spoons in three cups: one with hot water, one with cold water, and one empty at room temperature. After 2 minutes, the spoon in hot water feels warmest. Which mode of thermal energy transfer is primarily responsible for the spoon becoming warm?
options: Convection within the spoon
Radiation from the water to the spoon
Conduction through direct contact between the hot water and the spoon
Evaporation of water onto the spoon
questions.explanation: The spoon gains thermal energy mainly by conduction: thermal energy is transferred through direct contact from the hot water to the spoon. This energy then spreads through the metal spoon by conduction.

questions.question: Why are cooling fins on engines and electronics often painted black?
options: To look more attractive
To prevent rust
To increase the rate of cooling by radiation
To reduce weight
questions.explanation: Dull black surfaces are good emitters of radiation. Painting cooling fins black increases the rate at which they can emit thermal energy by radiation, helping to cool the component more effectively.

questions.question: Fibreglass is a material made of fine glass fibres with trapped air pockets. It is often used in building attics. Which statement best explains why fibreglass is suitable for this purpose?
options: Fibreglass is a good conductor of thermal energy
Fibreglass is a poor conductor of thermal energy, reducing thermal energy transfer through the roof
Fibreglass absorbs radiation and converts it to light
Fibreglass creates convection currents that cool the house
questions.explanation: Fibreglass is a poor conductor of thermal energy. The trapped air pockets also transfer thermal energy slowly. This reduces the rate of thermal energy transfer between the inside and outside of a building, helping to maintain comfortable indoor temperatures.

questions.question: In the 'cool roof' programme, why are light-coloured or reflective roofs recommended for buildings in hot climates?
options: Light colours conduct thermal energy better
Light colours absorb more solar radiation
Light colours reflect more solar radiation, reducing thermal energy gain
Light colours create stronger convection currents
questions.explanation: Light-coloured or reflective surfaces reflect more solar radiation and absorb less. This reduces the amount of thermal energy gained by the building, helping to keep indoor temperatures lower and reducing the need for air conditioning.

questions.question: Why does thermal expansion result in a change in density?
options: The mass of the substance changes when it expands
The volume changes while the mass stays the same, so density changes
Density is not related to thermal expansion
Only gases change density when heated
questions.explanation: Density equals mass divided by volume. When a substance expands, its volume increases while its mass stays the same. This causes the density to decrease. When it contracts, volume decreases and density increases.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares conduction and convection?
options: Both require a material medium, but only convection involves movement of the substance itself
Both can occur in a vacuum
Conduction occurs only in gases, convection occurs only in solids
Convection is faster than conduction in all materials
questions.explanation: Both conduction and convection require a material medium. Conduction transfers thermal energy through direct contact within a material. Convection transfers thermal energy through the movement of the fluid itself (liquids or gases) due to density differences.
